title: WPMS/1652/2020 of RAVI TOMAR Vs HINDUSTAN PETROLEUM CORPORATION LIMITED

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1652 of 2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Vibhor Maheshwari, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for
respondent no. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
Petitioner and respondent no. 2 both
had applied for setting up of a retail outlet
for petrol. A draw of lots was held, in
which respondent no. 2 was selected.
By means of this writ petition,
petitioner has sought following reliefs:
"A. Issue a writ in the nature of Certiorari
or issue any other appropriate writ,
direction or orders for quashing of
selection of respondent No. 2 via draw of
lots with respect of tender dated
25.11.2018 and all contractual and
reciprocal obligations arising therefrom in
so far as they relate to location being
"between Km stone no. 110 and 115, on
National Highway 72, Paonta Sahib to
Dharmawala Chowk Road, Dehradun,
Uttarakhand", given at Serial No. 60 of the
location-wise chart as published by
Respondent no. 1.
B. Issue a writ in the nature of Mandamus
or issue any other appropriate writ,
direction or orders to Respondent No. 1 for
carrying out a fresh draw of lots for the
remaining eligible applicants, including the
Petitioner, from the relevant group (Group
1) from which Respondent No. 2 was
wrongfully selected."
Learned counsel for the petitioner
has referred to one document, which is
enclosed as Annexure No. 7 to the writ
petition, wherein the Chief Regional
Manager, H.P.C.L. has stated that the
land offered by respondent no. 2 for

establishing the retail outlet, was not
found suitable, as per N.H.A.I. guidelines.
Based on the said admission,
learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that the retail outlet cannot be granted to
respondent no. 2.
Learned counsel for respondent no.
1 submits that, due to pandemic caused
by Covid-19, the Land Evaluation
Committee could not sit, however, he
submits that the process of evaluation
has been resumed from 01.10.2020. He
further assures the Court that the
meeting of the Land Evaluation
Committee would be held within fifteen
days from today and appropriate decision
shall be taken regarding suitability of the
land offered by respondent no. 2.
The decision taken by the Land
Evaluation Committee will be placed
before the Competent Authority within
three days and the Competent Authority
shall pass appropriate order, in
accordance with law, within one week
thereafter.
In view of the statement made by
learned counsel for respondent no. 1, the
writ petition stands disposed of.
Let a certified copy of this order be
issued within 24 hours.
